newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand wool prices generally ease at sales.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand wool prices generally ease at sales.

text.p: Wool prices generally eased at Thursday's sales in Christchurch and Napier, with the market indicator down 10 cents to 463 NZ cents per kg clean when compared to finalised prices from last Thursday's sale, Wools of New Zealand said.
The strong segment indicator fell eight cents to 387, while the medium segment rose three to 599 cents. The fine segment was down 55 cents to 977 cents.
Compared to the June 19 sale in Christchurch, prices for merino fleece were up to five percent cheaper, apart from 23 micron, which was two percent dearer.

Halfbred fleece prices were up to 1.5 percent dearer for 26 to 28 micron, but up to 1.5 percent cheaper for 29 to 32 micron. Crossbred fleece 36 micron and finer were up to two percent dearer, while 37 micron and stronger were up to 3.5 percent cheaper.

Second shear 33 to 35 micron were slightly cheaper and 37 micron 75/100 mm were unchanged. Second shear 37 micron shorter were 2.5 to five percent cheaper, while 38 micron and stronger were 2.5 to 3.5 percent cheaper.
Second lambs were unchanged. Bulky skirtings, second shear bellies and pieces and crutchings were all up to 2.5 percent cheaper.

Of the 3,913 clean tonnes on offer, 16 percent failed to meet growers' price reserves. The offer comprised 42 percent second shear, 15 percent crossbred fleece, 14 percent halfbred fleece and 10 percent second shear bellies and pieces.
The main bidding came from Western Europe, China, India and Pakistan. The next sales are at Christchurch and Napier on July 31. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
